audit.whatIsWrong: early states "Your Void Stone magic reduction does nothing here because all of Jayce's damage is physical". That is false: Thundering Blow, the hammer-stance E that the page names four separate times as the thing that kills you, deals MAGIC damage. Separately, the stance swap itself is never described anywhere - Mercury Cannon's first attack shreds the target's Armour AND Magic Resist and resets his attack, and Hextech Capacitor gives him Move Speed on every swap. And breakdown.late says to 'Q-silence the counterplay'; Null Sphere has no silence.
audit.why: The reader is told a defensive stat is worthless against the exact ability they are told to fear, when in fact Void Stone and the Q shield are the two things that blunt it. And the swap is the whole matchup: Mercury Cannon/Mercury Hammer is a SIX-SECOND cooldown, so a Jayce who has just fired a gated Shock Blast in cannon form cannot reach Thundering Blow for six seconds. That is the Riftwalk window, and it is far more actionable than 'is Shock Blast down?' because the swap is visible on his model rather than tracked in your head. The armour-and-MR shred on his first cannon attack is also the burst tell - the wind-up, not the ability cast.
audit.corrected: The all-physical claim replaced with the true split (cannon Q and autos physical, Thundering Blow magic); the 6s stance swap written in as the commit window; the Mercury Cannon resist-shred named as the tell; the silence removed.
sources: champ-data/_kits/jayce.json (E Hammer: 'Deals magic damage to an enemy and knocks them back'; R: 'The first attack in this form reduces the target's Armor and Magic Resist', cooldown 6, autoReset; P Hextech Capacitor: Move Speed on swap)

audit.whatIsWrong: Shock Blast is called matchup-defining in seven places and its cooldown appears nowhere. Neither does Thundering Blow's, nor the stance swap's.
audit.why: Shock Blast is 16/14/12/10/8/6s - sixteen seconds at rank 1, which is an enormous window for a champion whose whole plan is to walk up during it. Thundering Blow is 20/18/16/14/12/10s, longer still. The stance swap is a flat 6s. Riftwalk answers at 5/3.5/2s. Those four numbers turn 'close after it whiffs' into an actual schedule: a whiffed gated Shock Blast buys you sixteen seconds, and if he is still in cannon form he cannot knock you back for six of them.
audit.corrected: All four written into the spikes, mid and the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives Jayce six of seven stages and Skill the seventh, so no stage reads Kassadin - while late opens 'This is the whole reason you picked Kassadin' and whys[6] says you 'assassinate a no-resist Jayce'.
audit.why: Kassadin loses this 40.91% over 22 games, so a Jayce-heavy chart is the right overall shape. But 2+ items is the stage where both prose sources say the lane has turned, and the chart contradicts them.
audit.corrected: 2+ items flipped to Kassadin in both layers. Everything earlier left with Jayce.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer never mentions minions, though the full layer's cooldown block does say 'stand behind minions'. The two layers know different things.
audit.why: Shock Blast detonates upon hitting an enemy, so a minion between you and Jayce eats the poke that the entire early-game section tells you to simply absorb. That single positioning rule is the difference between conceding CS and farming the lane, and it lives only in a block the reader may never open.
audit.corrected: The minion-block written into early and the Lvl 1-3 spike where it belongs.
sources: champ-data/_kits/jayce.json (Q Cannon: 'Fires an orb of electricity that detonates upon hitting an enemy')

edits.before: Jayce owns these levels completely and there is no way around it. His cannon Shock Blast, fired through the Acceleration Gate, out-ranges everything you have, and stepping into Null Sphere range means eating a poke that hits like a truck — your Q shield blanks one shot but he just pokes you again before it comes back. Do not try to trade; last-hit at max range, take the chip, and accept you will lose CS and HP. Your Void Stone magic reduction does nothing here because all of Jayce's damage is physical.
edits.after: Jayce owns these levels completely. His cannon Shock Blast, fired through the Acceleration Gate, out-ranges everything you have - but it detonates on the first enemy it hits, so a minion between the two of you eats it. Stand behind the wave to last-hit instead of beside it. Do not try to trade; take the chip and accept you will lose CS. His cannon Q and his autos are physical, so Void Stone sleeps through the poke phase - but Thundering Blow, the hammer knockback, is magic, and that is the one hit your passive and Q shield genuinely blunt.

edits.before: Level 6 is your lifeline — Riftwalk finally gives you a way to blink out of his Thundering Blow knockback or sidestep a gated Shock Blast instead of just absorbing it. Use Nether Blade on minions to keep your mana topped so you can afford to Riftwalk defensively. You are still behind through 4-5, so keep farming under tower and only Q to interrupt or push a wave; do not blink in on a healthy Jayce — his burst still beats yours until your items come online.
edits.after: Level 6 is your lifeline - Riftwalk blinks you out of Thundering Blow or sidesteps a gated Shock Blast. Watch the weapon, not the cooldown bar: his stance swap is a flat 6 seconds, so a Jayce who just gated a Shock Blast in cannon form cannot reach the hammer to knock you away for six of them. That is your window. Use Nether Blade on minions to keep mana topped, keep farming under tower through 4-5, and never blink in on a healthy Jayce holding hammer.
